messages:
alex_mckinley: FYI quay scan flagged high severity CVEs in our base images (ubuntu:20.04 focal, alpine:3.16). OpenSSL CVE-2026-0001 and glibc CVE-2026-0002 showed up. Need quick triage and a patch/rebuild plan.

priya_singh: Can you paste exact image tags and whether these are used by hosted runtime or only Dedicated/Private?

alex_mckinley: Tags: `redwood-runtime:2026-03-10` (focal), `redwood-sidecar:alpine-3.16-2026-02-28`. Both are in Dedicated pools and used by some Private installs. Vulnerabilities: CVE-2026-0001 (openssl 1.1.1f -> upstream 1.1.1u backport available), CVE-2026-0002 (glibc bounds/heap issue).

jorge_almeida: Priority should be Dedicated runtime first, then sidecars, then local dev images. For glibc we probably need distro backports or move focal images to ubuntu:22.04 base (glibc newer).

samantha_cho: Quick triage checklist: 1) reproduce exploitability in our runtime container profile, 2) check whether any private keys/secrets were baked in images (KMS exposure), 3) confirm whether any SLSA/supply-chain artifacts are impacted.

secops-bot: New advisory: openssl 1.1.1u released, Alpine edge has patches. See https://security.example.com/advisories/openssl-2026 :warning:

priya_singh: Suggested phased approach: build patched images, run canary in dedicated-staging, smoke tests + fuzzing, then ramp 5% -> 25% -> full if no regression. Also update SBOMs.

alex_mckinley: Minimal Dockerfile patch to test upgrades: 
```Dockerfile
FROM ubuntu:20.04
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install --only-upgrade -y openssl libc6 && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
```

jorge_almeida: For Alpine sidecar, example: 
```sh
apk update && apk add --no-cache --upgrade openssl=1.1.1u-r0
```
We should also enable multi-arch builds in CI and add package pins to avoid accidental downgrades.

samantha_cho: Release/ops checklist: update CHANGELOG with vuln summary, publish SBOM, regenerate container signatures, rotate any keys if we discover secrets in image layers (we should not have any private keys baked).

alex_mckinley: Who owns coordinating the rebuild + release PRs? @priya_singh?

priya_singh: I can lead. Plan: start builds today, produce canary tags `redwood-runtime:2026-03-18-patched-canary` and `redwood-sidecar:alpine-patched-2026-03-18`. Need infra window for canary deploy.

jorge_almeida: I'll schedule a 2-node canary in `dedicated-staging` during 02:00-04:00 UTC. Monitoring: latency, error rate, KV cache hits, and tail p99. Rollout policy: 5% (smoke) -> 25% (staged) -> 100% (full) with 2h observation between steps.

deploy-bot: Scheduled deploy to dedicated-staging at 2026-03-18T02:15Z for image `redwood-runtime:2026-03-18-patched-canary`.

alex_mckinley: Also request KMS audit for any suspicious access around image build time. @secops-bot can you run a key-access audit for the last 30 days for build service account?

secops-bot: Running KMS access audit for `build-service-account` (30d). Will post anomalies to #incidents if found.

priya_singh: I'll open PRs in infra/ci to update Dockerfiles, add SBOM generation and CI gates. I'll link PRs here when created.

alex_mckinley: Also add a short playbook note in /docs/incident-response/vuln-remediation.md about when to patch base images vs. moving to newer distros (decision criteria: exploitability, backport availability, regression risk).

jorge_almeida: One more: ensure our regen of pinned images includes a rebuild of wheel caches so downstream layers are deterministic.

priya_singh: PRs opened: infra#1423 (ubuntu focal openssl/glibc upgrade), infra#1424 (alpine sidecar openssl pin). CI builds started. Will update with canary image tags.

alex_mckinley: Thanks team. We'll treat this as P2 (high severity, scheduled patch) and keep communication in this thread. If secops-bot finds KMS anomalies, escalate to #incidents immediately. :thumbsup:
